conviction_note: The H1 period is pre-released: revenue +12%, 11% organic, and an FY outlook of 'slightly ahead' came out in the 15 Oct trading update, which moved the stock +7.7% and is about +15% to date. What is left is the H1 margin against an easy comparator, which a primary document points up, and a large holder's exit that the market absorbed. Against that, the name has fallen on its last three results days (-6.8, -6.7, -2.2). So the findings sum to +0.6 and p_up stays at 50, giving a scaled 0.0 on an unsigned 3.5% move. The gap between the two numbers is the sell-the-print history, not a second view on the fundamentals.

findings.finding: The 15 Oct TU attributes FY profit being 'slightly ahead' to 'disciplined cost management and delivery of operating efficiencies' as well as revenue. The H1 margin is not yet disclosed and is set against a depressed H1 FY26 comparator (adj EBITDA margin 27.2% -> 26.0%, adj PBT only +5% on revenue +13%), the line on which the stock fell 6.7% last November.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: H1 FY26 (2025-11-20): margin down 120bp, adj PBT +5%, stock -6.69% over the window. FY25 results (2025-06-19), EPS miss: -6.78%
findings.why_not_priced: The TU gave revenue and an FY qualitative statement but no margin. The stock's +7.7% TU day and +15% drift partly price the FY profit upgrade, so only the H1-margin delta against last year's depressed comparator is left. If it were fully priced, the bar would carry a sourced H1 EBITDA consensus at a recovered margin, and none is published. That is why the finding is small.
findings.independence: The comparator margin is from a separate source, AJ Bell / Alliance News on the H1 FY26 print: https://www.ajbell.co.uk/news/articles/xps-confident-meeting-guidance-advisory-drives-first-half-growth (adj PBT +5.3% on revenue +13%)

findings.finding: Gresham House Asset Management cut its holding from 9.55% to 4.66% (threshold crossed 17 Nov, about 10m shares, roughly 5% of the company, on 3.4m and 2.5m share volume on 16-17 Nov), while Aberdeen rose from 8.0% to 9.07% on 11 Nov. The stock held at 352-356p through both, so a large seller has cleared before the print.
findings.why_not_priced: The TR-1 went out at 11:06 on the seal day and is not in wire previews. The absorption is visible on the tape (price flat on heavy volume), so the overhang removal is mostly priced, hence the small size. A seller exiting half a stake two days before results could also be read as informed, which is why the range runs negative.
findings.independence: Aberdeen's TR-1, a buyer at the same time: https://www.investegate.co.uk/announcement/rns/xps-pensions-group--xps/holding-s-in-company/9875185 ; volumes from https://query1.finance.yahoo.com/v8/finance/chart/XPS.L?range=3mo&interval=1d

baseline_tension: The small positive findings agree with the +1.7 priced lean and the +5% / +12.7% run-ups, and that agreement is part of why the scaled number is 0: a TU-driven 15% rally into a pre-released half and a three-print sell-the-results history leave nothing the price does not hold.
language_note: Nothing the English sources did not already carry. The domestic RNS channel (Investegate) supplied the primary documents (TU, TR-1s, results notice) that the wire stories paraphrase, and the only item absent from wire copy was the 18 Nov Gresham House TR-1, which is an RNS item rather than a locality difference.
lessons_applied: 'A finding about a number the market has already been told is worth 0' (reported_quarter 4/14 on pre-released periods): the margin finding went from +0.8 to +0.4, because the FY profit statement and its cost-discipline attribution were in the TU and only the H1 margin split is new

'A pre-released period with an unchanged guide sits between 45 and 55' and the reaction history moves p_up, not size: p_up went from 52 to 50, abs_move_pct held at 3.5 (3% base, nudged up for the $1-5m turnover band), print_vs_bar from +2.0 to +1.5
